Little background: want to get a pistol for my child, first pistol and possibly weapon he will use if he can practice and get on a local kids pistol league. I have little experience with .22 lr pistols ( besides the little cowboy style .22 i learned how to shoot and proper pistol safety with as a kid) and have some questions about some of the less expensive options on the market. I have narrowed it down to two options, the Beretta Neos and the Ruger Mark III. The biggest things to me are build quality, reliability and accuracy, as this is going to be a pistol i hope will be able to be used in the local youth firearm classes and pistol leagues. He is left handed, so how are these two pistols for the left handed shooter? Ambidextrous safety? Any input would be greatly appreciated!
Hard Choices, need input: Ruger Mark III vs. Beretta Neos
The Mark III is a bitch to clean. I'd go with the Beretta. The Browning Buck Mark is nice too, if you haven't considered it.

Maybe take him to the gun shop or a firing range where they have rentable guns, and let him handle them? I taught my kids using a Ruger Super Single Six (my rule was "you have to cock it each time, or I won't let you use it") just because it was single action. Also, I didn't want one of them shooting me in the foot. Or themselves.

I am left handed. I own a Beretta Neos pistol, and have shot Ruger Mark III, and 22/45 pistols.

The beretta neos is supremely easy to disassemble, clean, reassemble, and shoot. It's not light, and is a bit front weighty, so if he's really young, it might be too heavy for him. The only problem with it as a lefty pistol is the mag release. You simply can't hit it with your left hand. So I bring my right index finger up/over, and hit it with that. Hope this helps.
